page: Microsoft Azure D16s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The instance delivers 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for advanced vector and matrix operations via AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16) and Intel AMX (tile, int8), backed by 260 MB of L3 cache. It contains no bundled GPUs and does not include local disk storage, instead utilizing remote Premium Storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable mid-range computational capability alongside selective vector throughput strengths. The instance achieved average ratings in stress-ng compute (1950.79 single-core, 15986.8 multi-core) and Geekbench 6 (1853.0 single-core, 11424.0 multi-core). However, it ranked in the top 25 percent for single-threaded gzip compression at 31.24 GB/sec and Geekbench text processing at 2523.0. In memory and operational testing, it sustained 23.35 million Redis SET operations per second and 28.54 GB/sec in static web throughput. Large-language model inference on small (135M) models produced 332.76 tokens per second during text generation.

Without included ephemeral storage, the D16s_v6 requires network-attached managed disks for persistent storage needs. This trade-off separates compute scaling from high-IOPS local storage overhead. The configuration provides balanced resource density for web application backends, container orchestration nodes, Redis caching layers, compilation tasks, and enterprise line-of-business software.
